s1.syndrome_frame: Painless swelling in the supraclavicular region with gradual enlargement over six years
salient_findings: 4.0-cm diameter, round, firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area
Ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
key_facts: 32-year-old man
Six-year history of painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region
Swelling gradually enlarged from the size of an almond to that of a lime
No history of trauma, fever, or systemic illness
No weakness, numbness, or loss of function in the upper limb
Mass is 4.0-cm in diameter, round, firm, and non-tender
Mass is mobile in the medio-lateral direction
Ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass
Mass has well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
Lower border of the mass lies adjacent to the subclavian artery
Medial border of the mass abuts the carotid artery and external jugular vein

shortlist.label: Branchial cleft cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound and cystogram findings corroborate this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the location and mobile nature of the mass

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, non-tender mass with gradual enlargement over six years

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, lymphoma cannot be entirely ruled out without further testing

raw.rationale: The ultrasound findings of a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa, along with the cystogram findings, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cystic lymphangioma
rejected.why: While possible, the location and ultrasound characteristics are more typical of a branchial cleft cyst.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid, not cystic, and do not usually have intralesional septa.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are benign fatty tumors that do not match the cystic appearance on ultrasound.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would likely present with systemic symptoms and multiple lymph node involvement, not a single, slowly enlarging mass.
